why_next: The Bayesian paradigm passes C1+C3 on the synthetic 12-state SPA, becoming the first valid estimator after 4 families failed. However, all evidence is synthetic SPA simulation — the claim ceiling explicitly excludes C-WEB-DYNAMICS and real Web data. The next materially orthogonal question is whether the estimator generalizes from synthetic state_id labels to genuine browser-derived URL state representations on TodoMVC hash-SPAs (leveraging EXP-PHYSICS-35209110569 infrastructure that validated hash-SPAs as suitable testbeds with 0.21-0.28 valid-only leakage). This tests a different dimension (synthetic→real state representation) rather than repeating the same synthetic SPA paradigm at larger N.

recommended_action: Execute Bayesian model comparison on real TodoMVC hash-SPA transitions (leveraging EXP-PHYSICS-35209110569 infrastructure: 5 variants, <40% leakage, NL 357-394). Use same K=12 Dirichlet-Multinomial, alpha {0.5,1.0,2.0}, within-session shuffled-action null with N_SHUFFLE>=1000. URL-level state representation (fragment-aware) instead of synthetic state_id. This tests the materially orthogonal question of synthetic→real generalization. If Bayesian approach passes C1+C3 on TodoMVC, it establishes the estimator on genuine browser transitions and opens the path to production SPA testing. If it fails, the synthetic→real gap is identified as the binding bottleneck and the Physics lane should consider continuous-state estimators (KDE/kNN on embeddings) or richer state representations.
